title: Asset Field Schema
description: Contract emitted by the decoder-agent and consumed by the rule-agent. Describes the fields a custom Wazuh decoder extracts from one asset's logs.

asset.description: Short slug for the asset/product, e.g. 'cisco-asa', 'paloalto-panos', 'mysql'. Used in file names and decoder names.

display_name.description: Human-readable product name, e.g. 'Cisco ASA Firewall'.

log_format.description: Detected top-level format of the log lines.

decoder_file.description: Path to the generated Wazuh decoder XML, e.g. 'database/decoders/cisco-asa_decoder.xml'.

sample_count.description: Number of raw log lines analysed to build this schema.

prematch.description: The decoder prematch expression used to identify this asset's logs (verbatim as written in the XML).

fields.description: Every field the decoder extracts, in decode order.

name.description: Field name as it appears to rules. Use Wazuh standard names where they apply (srcip, dstip, srcport, dstport, srcuser, dstuser, action, protocol, id, url, status). Otherwise a dynamic field referenced in rules as data.<name>.

wazuh_field.description: How a rule references this field: a standard tag (e.g. 'srcip') or 'data.<name>' for a dynamic field.

type.description: Semantic type, used by the rule-agent to pick detections and comparators.

example.description: A real value pulled from the sample logs.

description.description: What the field means in this product's context.

security_relevant.description: Hint from the decoder-agent that this field is worth alerting on (auth result, command, src/dst, action, severity).

enum_values.description: Observed distinct values when the field is categorical (e.g. action: ['allow','deny','drop']).

event_kinds.description: Distinct event types the decoder-agent observed (e.g. 'authentication failure', 'connection denied', 'config change'). Seeds the rule-agent's detection ideas.

message_id.description: Product message/event ID if present (e.g. Cisco ASA '%ASA-4-106023').

notes.description: Free-form caveats: ambiguous fields, multi-line handling, encodings, fields that vary by event kind.
